prose: Kotaku reports that hundreds of vibe-coded, AI-decompiled emulators and games have appeared in the past couple of weeks, playable in browser tabs: Black Ops zombies, Skate 3, Halo, Modern Warfare 2, GTA: Vice City and The Simpsons: Hit and Run among them.

The trigger, per the piece, is that Claude's latest update, Claude Opus 5.5, is extremely good at decompiling, so reconstructing a game's source now takes a fraction of the months it used to take coders. The wave also includes native Fallout and Call of Duty ports and AI-generated mash-up mods like Super Mario 64 inside Elden Ring. The legal blowback is presumably coming; read the original for the full picture.
highlights: Hundreds of AI-decompiled games playable in browsers
Claude Opus 5.5 singled out as the decompiling engine
Months of reverse engineering compressed to days
Halo, GTA: Vice City, Skate 3, Black Ops among the ports
Mash-up mods like Mario 64 in Elden Ring cited
